newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-BRACKEN SUMMONED FROM HOLIDAY TO JOIN LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BRACKEN SUMMONED FROM HOLIDAY TO JOIN LIONS.

text.p: England scrumhalf Kyran Bracken was summoned from a Caribbean holiday on Sunday to join the British Lions as the replacement for injured Welshman Rob Howley on their South African tour.

Bracken had been enjoying the first day of a holiday in Tobago, unaware that the Lions wanted him to replace Howley who dislocated his left shoulder during the Lions' 42-12 victory over Natal at Kings Park on Saturday.
British Lions selectors telephoned Mike Scott, administration manager of Bracken's Saracens club in London. He initiated frantic efforts to track down the player, who had left no contact number.
Scott telephoned 13 hotels on Tobago before he found Bracken, who becomes the third player from Saracens to come in as a 1997 Lions replacement.
Saracens prop Paul Wallace replaced Ireland's Peter Clohessy and number eight Tony Diprose arrived in South Africa for Welshman Scott Quinnell last week.
Bracken, who made his England debut against New Zealand in 1993, received a belated recall to the England side which drew the recent test series 1-1 in Argentina.
Howley was set to fly back to Britain on Sunday night, Lions media liaison officer Bob Burrows said. He is expected to be out of the game for four months.
